hook_text: Why is South Africa's biggest city not on the coast or a big river?
clip_script: Johannesburg: eGoli, the place of gold. On a floor map, a class sticks on symbols. Yellow triangles for gold, in an arc through Gauteng, North West and the Free State. Black squares for coal in Mpumalanga. Grey circles for platinum around Rustenburg. Red for iron ore in the Northern Cape. Then they mark the towns, and they sit right on top of the mines. Johannesburg grew because of gold. Mines make towns.
visual_style: Whiteboard outline of South Africa filling with coloured mining symbols, then town dots appearing on top of them.
mood: Curious and clever, like solving a map puzzle.
pacing: Symbol by symbol, then the big reveal of the towns.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the nearest mine to your town on a map.
